headline: 褒める, “to praise”, comes from Old Japanese 褒む (pomu).
ベル is the English word “bell” in katakana.
こちらこそ is こちら (kochira, “this person, I”) plus こそ (koso, “it is… that”).
バランス is borrowed from English “balance”.
リズム is borrowed from English “rhythm”.
謝る, “to apologize”, is from 誤る (ayamaru, “mistake”).
オフィス is the English word “office” in katakana.
訪ねる, “to visit”, comes from the Old Japanese verb 訪ぬ (tadunu).
クーラー, “air conditioner”, is borrowed from English “cooler”, first cited to 1959.
ぶつぶつ, “grumbling in a small voice”, is described simply as onomatopoeic.
マイク is the English word “mic” in katakana.
列, “queue, line, row”, is from Middle Chinese 列 (ljet).
パートタイム is the English word “part-time” in katakana.
レポート is the English word “report” in katakana.
治める is from Old Japanese 治む (wosamu), and the source gives 収める (osameru) as a cognate.
リボン is borrowed from English “ribbon”.
冷める comes from the classical verb 冷む (samu).
メッセージ is the English word “message” in katakana.
決まり is the continuative stem of the verb 決まる (kimaru, “to be decided, to be concluded”).
ダム is borrowed from English “dam”.
愛, “love”, comes from Middle Chinese, and the source points to Mandarin ài for comparison.
ランチ is borrowed from English “lunch”.
サークル is borrowed from English “circle”.
まあまあ is a reduplication of まあ, and its likeness to a Cantonese “so-so” phrase is likely coincidental.
ビニール is the English word “vinyl” in katakana.
それなら is それ (“that”) plus なら (“if”): literally “if that”.
モダン is borrowed from English “modern”.
信じる is a shift from 信ずる (shinzuru).
リットル, “liter”, is borrowed from French “litre”.
ジュース covers “juice” and “deuce”, each borrowed from its own English word.
